correctness.rationale: For every d>=3, exact plane maximizing a rank-one spike gives ratio 1-(p.x)^2. Conditional spherical isotropy yields iid Beta((d-2)/2,1/2) factors, with an explicit gamma-moment identity. At k=floor(cd), the scaled log-MGF converges on theta<1/2 to -(c/2)log(1-2theta), and the tilted variance is O(1/d); matching exponential upper/lower bounds and exponential tightness give the full rate I_c(s) for s>0 and infinity otherwise. Correct boundaries and finite-step positivity verified. An independent matrix-eigensolver script returned VERIFY_OK with 320 direct updates, 12 moment comparisons and 12 rate checks; it is not relied upon as asymptotic proof.

originality.rationale: The October 30 2026 source Example 2.4 already gives the exact spiked spectral ascent and expectation, while Proposition 2.5 uses Beta spherical caps for a different hitting-time upper bound. The new assertion is the sharp dimension-scale LDP and both matched tail exponents, obtained by finite-d gamma moments and a nontrivial joint d,k limit; these do not follow from its displayed expected factor or generic tail upper bound without an additional distributional and tilted-exponent argument. The earlier 2024/2025 papers address different types of convergence. Query results for one-shot ellipsoid sections, spectral filtering, and random-pivot products do not logically imply this result. Unpublished or unlocated specialized Beta-product applications remain a priority risk.
